# Chapter 4: The God's Demand

**Applying Guy Sclanders' Methodology**

<details>
<summary><strong>Session Overview</strong></summary>

Session 3 ended with the party leaving the fort, Lucius dead, moving south through the
forest. They know from S3 intel that the dungeon lies beyond the Farbog -- a glowing
green marsh south of a Germanic village. Vercingetorix is an enemy, not a guide; he
fought them at the fort and is not with the party.

This session is the journey to that dungeon's door, not the dungeon itself. The party
crosses the Farbog, reaches the Germanic village where Thusnelda leads what remains of
his people, visits the sacred grove to the north, and then confronts the session's real
dramatic engine: Thusnelda, standing in the ritual sacrifice circle near the grove,
preparing to give his own life because he believes that is what will end the bloodshed.
He is wrong. The party must stop him, or fail to, before they can even reach the dungeon
entrance. The session ends after the Bone Naga fight at the dungeon entrance, with the
party stepping into the Ossuary. They advance to Level 6.

**Level:** 5 throughout → advance to 6 at session end (after the Ossuary)
**Duration:** 4--5 hours
**Key Goal:** Cross the Farbog, reach the village, stop Thusnelda's sacrifice, enter the dungeon, clear the Ossuary
**Theme:** Devotion is not the same as truth. Good people do terrible things for honest reasons.

<details>
<summary><strong>Guy Sclanders' Principles Applied</strong></summary>

- **Strong Opening:** Start mid-movement. The party is already in the bog, not walking toward it.
- **Never Present Villain, Now Felt:** The cult's corruption is visible before the dungeon door. The sacrifice circle shows what the cult's blood-magic did to ordinary Germanic faith.
- **Pressure Cooker:** Thusnelda's ritual has a clock. She has been in that circle since dawn. The party doesn't have unlimited time to talk.
- **Three Clue Rule:** Three independent confirmations this dungeon is the right target -- supply caches at the marsh, cult markings on the sacrifice circle stones, Thusnelda's knowledge of where the chieftains went.
- **Meaningful Choices:** Do they stop Thusnelda by force, by argument, or not at all? All three paths have real consequences.

</details>

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 0: The Farbog Crossing</strong></summary>

The party arrives at the Farbog -- a wide marsh glowing cold green in daylight. A bone
causeway runs across it. At the far side, the hillside opens in a carved skull twenty
feet tall. Before the causeway begins, a standing stone rises from the bank.

**Read aloud:**

> *The trees end and the ground turns to black water. Ahead, a causeway of old skulls
> and packed bone runs across the marsh toward a hillside that has a face -- a skull
> carved from the living rock, easily twenty feet across, its eye sockets dark even now.
> The water on either side glows green. Not fire. Something slower, like a pulse.*
>
> *At the bank's edge, a standing stone. Runes cut deep. Old work -- older than the
> causeway. Someone wanted something remembered here.*

---

**The Standing Stone -- Riddle for Reward**

DC 13 Intelligence (History) to read the Germanic runes. Read aloud to the player who succeeds:

> *"Born from the willing, fed by the blood, I grow in the silence where no god has
> stood. Worship without truth, devotion without cost -- I am what remains after the
> believer is lost. Name me."*

The answer is **the hunger** -- or any answer meaning "hollow faith," "false devotion," or "the cult's work." A character who names it correctly (or any answer the DM judges honest and insightful) finds a carved bone token hidden in a notch at the stone's base.

::: {.dm-note}
**Bone Token reward:** grants one free reroll on any saving throw against an undead ability for the rest of the session. One use, no attunement. The rune on it is OTHALAN -- the same mark from Session 1's vault. A character who recognises it (DC 11 Intelligence (History), or automatic if they handled the Session 1 contract token) knows this symbol has been here longer than the cult. Something pre-dates the chieftains' work.
:::

---

**Avoidance -- the quiet crossing**

The Wights are dormant while the glowing water is undisturbed. They sense warmth and
movement in the water, not on the bone causeway itself. If the party moves slowly and
stays on the causeway, they may pass without waking them.

**DC 14 group Dexterity (Stealth) check** -- more than half must succeed. On success: the
party crosses in silence, Wights never rise, no combat. On failure -- or if anyone
steps into the water: the Wights rise as the party is mid-crossing.

::: {.dm-note}
Let the party try the riddle and choose their approach before revealing the avoidance
option explicitly. A player who asks "can we sneak past?" gets the Stealth check. A
player who just walks gets the encounter. Reward attention.
:::

---

**Why the Wights are here**

The cult's two chieftains demanded a test of devotion before any follower could approach
the dungeon. Early converts were ordered to stand guard in the bog overnight, in the
water, alone. The ones who failed -- who left the water, who drowned, who broke --
never came home. The cult magic that fed on their deaths bound them here. They did not
choose to stay. They were never given a choice about leaving.

**Supply caches:** Two low stone walls at the near shore hold crates and barrels. DC 11 Wisdom (Investigation): rations gone green with the same glow, a tally stick (the cult has been here many months), and a torn strip of cloth in the two chieftains' warband colours.

---

**Encounter: 3 × Wight** (*Monster Manual* p. 300 -- CR 3, AC 14, HP 45) rise from
the black water when disturbed.

::: {.dm-note}
**Wight stats (official MM):**
- *Longsword:* +4 to hit, 1d8+2 slashing (or 1d10+2 two-handed)
- *Longbow:* +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., 1d8+2 piercing
- *Life Drain:* +4 to hit, 1d6+2 necrotic, DC 13 Constitution save or HP maximum reduced by damage taken until long rest. On a kill, target rises as a Zombie under the Wight's control.
- **Sunlight Sensitivity:** disadvantage on attack rolls and Perception in sunlight -- it is daytime, this applies. They fight at disadvantage in the open.
- **Terrain:** Wights rise from the water flanking the causeway. They cannot step onto it easily -- treat the causeway edges as difficult terrain for them. The party has the high ground.

**If a PC dies here:** they rise as a Zombie at the start of the next round unless the Wight is destroyed first or the body is moved off the causeway immediately. Say this plainly before combat starts -- it is not a cheap surprise.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 1: The Germanic Village</strong></summary>

Past the Farbog, the forest opens into a Germanic settlement -- longhouses around a
central fire pit, fewer people than the buildings suggest. Thusnelda is not here; he
left at dawn for the grove.

**Read aloud:**

> *The village smells of woodsmoke and old bread. Chickens. A dog that barks once and
> stops. Two fires burning where ten should be. The longhouses are solid work, well-kept,
> but half the doors stand open on empty rooms. A woman stops grinding grain and watches
> you without moving. A child runs inside. An old man at the fire does not look up.*
>
> *Whatever took this village apart, it was not a raid. Raiders leave bodies and ash.
> This place just... thinned.*

**What the villagers know (if approached without threat):**

- The grove is to the north. The dungeon entrance is to the south, past the old
  offering stones.
- Their seer -- an older man, name of Thusnelda -- went to the grove alone before dawn.
  Three people followed and came back frightened. He would not stop or explain himself.
- The two chieftains "went south" months ago and never returned. The villagers stopped
  asking about them.
- DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion): a villager says Thusnelda has spoken of "settling the
  gods' debt" for two weeks. No one knew what he meant until this morning when he took
  a blade with him.

::: {.dm-note}
**Thusnelda's reputation:** DC 13 Intelligence (History) or DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) while talking to villagers -- a PC learns Thusnelda is of old blood, a trained völva whose family has read the omens in this forest for generations. He is not reckless. He is not suicidal. He has been right about everything for twenty years. That is what makes this dangerous.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 2: The Sacred Grove</strong></summary>

North of the village, a stand of ancient oaks around a stone shrine. The Belatucadrus
shrine the party may have heard of in Session 3 is here -- a weathered stone face, not
quite Roman Mars, not quite Germanic Tiwaz.

**Read aloud:**

> *The oaks here are old enough that their roots have lifted the path. At the grove's
> center, a stone no taller than a man stands alone, its face carved on the side facing
> the village -- two faces, really, or one face trying to be two. Roman workmanship on
> top, older marks underneath. Someone has left fresh holly. Someone else has smeared
> ash across the Roman features.*

**What the shrine tells them:** DC 13 Intelligence (Religion): this is Belatucadrus --
the Celtic sun god the Romans renamed Mars on the frontier. The ash over the Roman
features is recent and deliberate. Someone is angry at the Roman overlay, not the god
underneath.

**What this means for the session:** a weapon consecrated here by a cleric or druid (10
minutes of prayer, no spell slot required) gains the *Belatucadrus blessing* for the
rest of the session -- advantage on damage rolls against creatures marked by the blood
cult's magic, and the weapon counts as magical for the Ossuary encounter.

::: {.dm-note}
**The standing stone circle:** Just past the shrine, through a gap in the oaks, is a
ring of seven standing stones. That is where Thusnelda is. The party can see him from
here before he sees them. Give them one round of observation before he notices.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 3: The Ritual Sacrifice Circle</strong></summary>

This is the session's dramatic centrepiece. Thusnelda stands in the centre of the stone
circle, barefoot, a ritual knife in his right hand and his left wrist already scored.
He is bleeding, but not yet fatally. He has a clear, calm purpose. He is not being
coerced. He is not confused. He has thought about this for weeks.

**Read aloud:**

> *He stands in the centre of the ring with the stillness of someone who has made up
> his mind. His feet are bare on the cold stone. The knife in his hand is old work --
> older than him, older than the village. His left wrist is scored, blood running down
> his fingers and dropping into the earth. He is watching it fall.*
>
> *He hears you come and does not look up.*
>
> *"You are too late to stop the debt. But you can witness. A willing death settles what
> war begins. The gods will be satisfied. Your soldiers will stop burning our grain."*

**What Thusnelda believes (false, but sincerely):**

The blood cult's months of ritual south of the village have left a divine debt -- a
hunger in the land. He has interpreted this as a sign that the gods require a willing
sacrifice to close the wound. He believes his own death will satisfy Mars and reduce
Roman aggression on the frontier. He is a völva; he has read omens correctly for
twenty years. This is the one time he is reading them wrong, because the cult
*poisoned* the local spiritual landscape to feed something else, and he cannot
distinguish the cult's manufactured hunger from a genuine divine demand.

**What is actually true:** The dungeon to the south is the source. The cult created the
hunger. His sacrifice will accomplish nothing except his death. Mars will still be
hungry. The Romans will still burn grain. And the party will lose their best living
guide to what is happening in this forest.

---

**Running the intervention:** the party has three paths.

<details>
<summary><strong>Path A: Persuasion (with evidence)</strong></summary>

If the party shows Thusnelda physical evidence that the cult, not the gods, is the
source of the hunger -- the cult cloth from the marsh cache, the tally stick, a cult
symbol from the fort attack -- he will listen. DC 14 Charisma (Persuasion).

On success: he lowers the knife. He does not believe them entirely -- he cannot undo
weeks of his own interpretation in one conversation -- but he stops. *"Show me the
place you describe. If the hunger ends when you unmake it, then I was wrong. I will
wait."*

On failure: he finishes the ritual. He does not die immediately -- a sacrificial
bloodletting of this kind takes time. The party has one more round to act before the
wound becomes fatal.

**Physical evidence advantage:** showing cult cloth, tally stick, or a cult symbol from the fort attack grants advantage on the roll.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Path B: Persuasion (without evidence)</strong></summary>

DC 18 Charisma (Persuasion). Very hard. He has been thinking about this longer than
the party has been in this forest. A character with the Outlander or Hermit background
may add their proficiency bonus to the check a second time (double proficiency) because
they understand how this kind of conviction forms.

On failure: same as Path A failure.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Path C: Physical intervention</strong></summary>

A character can grab his arm or knock the knife away. This requires a successful grapple
or Disarm (Athletics or Acrobatics DC 13, contested by his Dexterity). He does not
fight back with the knife -- he will not harm the party -- but he will struggle. If
grappled, he says:

> *"You do not understand what you are preventing. Let go of me."*

He stops fighting if held long enough to hear the Persuasion argument. Use this as a
bridge to Path A, not a replacement for it. If the party physically restrains him and
says nothing, he simply waits -- and the party must eventually decide what to do with
a tied-up völva who still believes he is right.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Path D: The party does not intervene</strong></summary>

Thusnelda completes the ritual. He does not die instantly -- a sacrificial bloodletting
of this type causes death in roughly an hour without magical healing. A PC who casts
*Cure Wounds* or *Healing Word* in that window can save him.

If he dies: the party loses their best source of local knowledge about what the cult did
to this land. The grove shrine loses its Belatucadrus blessing. In Session 5, any check
to understand the dungeon's purpose is made without the context Thusnelda could have
provided.

His death does not stop the cult. The land's hunger does not ease. Everything he
sacrificed himself for fails to happen, exactly as the party (if they understood the
situation) would have predicted.

</details>

---

::: {.dm-note}
**On playing Thusnelda:** he is not a villain. He is not deluded in a dismissable way.
He is intelligent, experienced, and has read the spiritual landscape of this forest for
his entire life. The cult corrupted that landscape so thoroughly that his reading is
genuinely off, and he has no way to know it. Play him as someone who is completely
right about everything except the one thing that matters. His calm is not a performance.
His willingness to die is not a symptom of despair. He believes he is the only person
brave enough to do what the gods require.

If the party stops him and then succeeds in the dungeon -- if the hunger ends -- he
will come to the dungeon mouth when they emerge and stand in silence for a long moment.
He will not apologise. He will say: *"The debt is paid. Not the way I thought."*
That is enough.
:::

**After the scene:** whether saved or having chosen to wait, Thusnelda tells the party
what he knows: the dungeon entrance is south through the standing stones, down the old
offering path. The chieftains used it. He has not gone himself because he knew what
the path meant. He gives them one more piece of information freely:

> *"The first room below has been making the dead stay. Do not let the bones on the
> floor fool you -- someone sorted them. Someone is still proud of that work."*

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 4: The Dungeon Entrance  ★ COMBAT</strong></summary>

South of the standing stone circle, past the old offering path, the hillside opens in a
carved skull twenty feet across. The stairs descend from between its teeth. The Bone
Nagas are coiled just inside -- guardians placed here precisely because this is the only
way in.

**Read aloud:**

> *The offering path ends at a hillside that has a face. A skull carved from the living
> rock, its eye sockets dark even at midday. Inside its mouth, stairs descend into
> darkness. The air coming up is cold and smells of old blood. And at the base of the
> stairs, two shapes uncoil from the stone -- serpentine, skeletal, moving with a
> purpose that bones alone do not explain.*

DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) (active: checking the entrance archway before
descending): cult markings cut into the stone around the skull's teeth -- the same
pattern as the cloth from the marsh cache. This is the right place.

**Encounter:** 2 × **[Bone Naga](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16812-bone-naga)** (*Monster Manual* p. 233 -- CR 4, AC 15, HP 58) at the base of the entrance stairs, plus 4 × **[Skeleton](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17015-skeleton)** (*Monster Manual* p. 272 -- CR 1/4, AC 13, HP 13) that animate from scattered bones on initiative count 20.

::: {.dm-note}
**Combat:**
- **Skeletons:** vulnerability to bludgeoning (MM p. 272). One hit from a mace or warhammer destroys them.
- **Bone Naga spellcasting** (DC 12 save, +4 attack): *hold person*, *ray of sickness* (2d8 poison), *ray of enfeeblement*. Bite: +5 to hit, 2d6+3 piercing + 4d6 poison (DC 11 Con save, half on success).
- **Terrain:** the entrance stairway is narrow -- only two characters can fight abreast. The Nagas use this, forcing the party to push down one at a time while the Skeletons flank from behind if anyone retreats up the stairs.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 5: The Ossuary  ★ SESSION 4 ENDS HERE</strong></summary>

Past the skull entrance, beyond the fallen Nagas, the dungeon proper begins. The first
room is circular. No combat. This is what the party finds when they finally get inside.

**Read aloud:**

> *The room ahead is round, and its far wall is shaped like the thing you just walked
> through -- another skull, smaller, teeth picked out in inlaid bone. The floor is a
> carpet of femurs and ribs. Not scattered. Sorted -- by size, by age, stacked with a
> care that took someone a very long time. Deeper in the dungeon, something breathes.*

DC 13 Intelligence (History) (active: examining the arrangement): these are not war
dead. They are curated -- months of deliberate work. Whoever sorted these bones was
proud of it. This matches the tally stick from the marsh.

There is a short passage at the far end leading deeper. The party can see nothing past
the first bend. Session 4 ends here.

::: {.dm-note}
**Level advancement:** party advances to **Level 6** after this session. Run it as a
break, not an in-fiction event -- they are still inside. Session 5 opens at this
threshold, at the edge of the Blood-Growth Rooms.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>DM Notes</strong></summary>

<details>
<summary><strong>OGAS This Session</strong></summary>

**Thusnelda** *(Scenes 1, 2, 3)*
- **Objective:** End the divine hunger he believes is consuming his people's future.
- **Goal:** Complete the sacrificial rite at the standing stone circle before anyone stops him.
- **Agenda:** He acts regardless of party interference -- he started at dawn and the party finds him mid-ritual. He will not rush, but he will not stop voluntarily without convincing argument or physical restraint.
- **Secret:** He has also been trying to find the cult's dungeon for three months. He could not locate it. He assumed that meant the gods wanted a different answer. He was looking for the entrance in the wrong direction.

**The Bone Nagas** *(Scene 4)*
- **Objective:** Guard the Ossuary.
- **Goal:** Kill intruders.
- **Agenda:** Coiled, dormant until movement detected. No tactics beyond what the stat block provides.
- **Secret:** The careful arrangement of the bones was done by the cult chieftains personally, room by room, as their own form of devotion. The Nagas were placed here to ensure it was never disturbed.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Session 4 → Session 5 handoff</strong></summary>

| Question | Session 5 implication |
|---|---|
| Is Thusnelda alive? | If yes: he waits at the dungeon mouth. Possible source of context for S5. If no: party enters S5 without local knowledge of the cult's history in this forest. |
| Was the Belatucadrus shrine blessed? | If yes: one PC carries a consecrated weapon into S5. Tell them it matters but not how yet. |
| What is each PC's corruption level? | The sacrifice circle has a minor passive field -- any PC at corruption 3+ who stood inside the circle for more than one round takes 1 temporary corruption point (no save, ambient). |
| Did the party find all three confirmations (cloth, tally stick, cult markings at entrance)? | If they missed one, leave it findable in the Blood-Growth Rooms at the start of S5. |

</details>
